title: The upper blade's sink is the weaker one in IED+ and high-knockout mice
why: In controls the two blades' sinks are about equal; in all five IED+ mice the lower blade's sink is the larger, in two of them by a wide margin. It needs no classifier, holds on both event sets, shows in the high-knockout, dose and trend contrasts too, and the averaged curves say the same thing (IED+ against IED−, cluster P = 0.007 at the upper sink). A blade-specific change is biologically specific: it would point at where the knockout cells are, or at one entorhinal input being hit harder.
against: The balance also depends on where the probe crosses the two blades, and it tracks the year of recording (rho +0.49): three controls were recorded in 2025 with what may be a different placement. IED+ mice are the high-knockout mice, so IED status and dose cannot be told apart here.
test: Fix the measure as defined here. In new mice, confirm probe position in both blades histologically and map knockout cells per blade; test IED+ against control (one planned test).

title: Dentate spikes are more uniform in size in IED+ mice
ylabel: CV of sink size across events
why: Every IED+ mouse has a lower event-to-event spread of sink size than every control (complete separation), and lower than every IED− mouse. The detector's own peak size shows the same (CV, P = 0.003, and 0.006 on the other event set), so it is not one way of measuring the sink. Uniform, stereotyped events are what a hypersynchronous dentate would produce.
against: Only events inside each recording's detection border are in the set; a border drawn tighter gives a narrower spread of sizes. Weaker on the No P-spikes set (P = 0.03). Five IED+ mice.
test: Recompute on all detected dentate spikes with one fixed detection threshold for every mouse, so the border cannot shape the spread.

title: The source-to-sink ratio varies more from event to event in PTEN mice
ylabel: CV across events of source / sink
why: The most consistent group difference in the battery: same sign and raw P under 0.05 in seven contrasts, and stronger on the No P-spikes set (P = 0.002). No classifier involved. If the return current at the granule cell layer is less tightly tied to the dendritic sink, the cells' passive or inhibitory response to the same input is less regular, which fits enlarged, heterogeneous knockout cells among normal ones.
against: A ratio's spread grows when the sink in the denominator is small or noisy, and sinks are smaller in several PTEN mice (lead 8). The source rows are landmarks from the mean event; if the source moves between events the ratio varies for that reason.
test: Repeat with the ratio taken only on events whose sink is above a fixed size, and with the source integrated over the whole space between the blades instead of at the landmark rows.

title: Source and sink peak less tightly together in high-knockout mice
ylabel: SD across events of (source peak time − sink peak time)
why: The jitter between the time the sink peaks and the time the source peaks is larger in high-knockout mice, rises with knockout over all mice (rho +0.69) and holds on both event sets. It is the timing counterpart of lead 3 and was measured independently of it (times, not sizes).
against: Tracks the year of recording (rho −0.48). Peak times are read to the millisecond on single events, so smaller events (lead 8) give noisier peak times by themselves.
test: Match events on sink size across groups before taking the jitter; if the difference stays, it is not a size effect.

title: The net source between the blades falls as the knockout rises
ylabel: Net CSD between the main sinks / sink size, median over events
why: This is the lead from the first pass, measured again with new code, per event instead of on the mean, and on both event sets: within PTEN, rho = −0.77. Under type-specific versions it is the strongest dose effect in the battery (rho −0.97 for one classifier, same sign under all of them). A weaker source at the granule cell layer for the same sink is what a loss of perisomatic return current, or a change in inhibition at the cell bodies, would look like.
against: Group difference against control is weak (high knockout against control P = 0.06); it is a dose relation among nine mice with no mice between 5% and 19% knockout, so it is two clusters. The source measure depends on how much of the hilus the probe crosses.
test: Mice with intermediate knockout (5-19%) are what this needs; one planned Spearman test within PTEN.

title: The events split less cleanly into two types in IED+ mice
ylabel: Second eigenvalue of the sink-overlap matrix
why: A classifier-free measure of how cleanly a recording's events fall into two groups. It is lower in every IED+ mouse than in every IED− mouse with a value, falls with knockout within PTEN (rho −0.83), and holds on both event sets. It agrees with the summary table: DS1 and DS2 are separable in 3 of 4 IED− mice, 1 of 5 IED+ mice and 2 of 8 controls. A loss of the DS1 / DS2 distinction in the mice with epileptiform activity would be a notable result.
against: IED− and low knockout are the same mice bar one. m7 has no value (the matrix has an isolated event). Controls are mostly not separable either, so this is not 'PTEN loses separability': IED− mice are the unusual ones. Whether a recording is separable also depends on whether the band reaches the outer sinks.
test: Widen the analyzed band so the outer sinks are inside it on every recording, re-extract, and test separability (yes / no by the fixed 0.45 rule) between IED+ and IED− in new mice.

title: The main sink sits farther from the source in IED+ mice
why: Modest statistically, but it is the one measure with a direct anatomical prediction: PTEN-knockout granule cells have longer dendrites and a thicker molecular layer, which should move the synaptic sink away from the cell-body source. The direction is right, it is the same on both event sets, and it rises control < IED− < IED+.
against: A probe crossing the layers at a slant lengthens every distance, and the angle is not known per mouse. Where there is one source between the blades the 'source' is the hilus midpoint, not each blade's granule layer. P = 0.03 uncorrected.
test: Measure the molecular layer's thickness and the probe's angle in histology for these same mice; the lead predicts the CSD distance follows the histological one.

title: Sinks are smaller in PTEN mice, most clearly in the IED− mice
ylabel: Upper-blade sink at the DS peak, median over events
why: The plain size of the upper blade's sink is lower in PTEN than control and lowest in the IED− mice (all four below seven of eight controls), identical on both event sets. A smaller dentate spike in the mice without epileptiform activity, and not in those with it, is the opposite of a simple 'more knockout, more excitable' story, which makes it worth a look.
against: Absolute size depends on electrode impedance and on how close the track runs to the layer; nothing normalizes that. Four IED− mice. The mean of both blades is weaker (P = 0.02) and the lower blade alone shows nothing.
test: Compare sizes within mouse across sessions first (is it stable?), then between groups with impedance recorded.

title: DS2 events follow each other within a second more often in PTEN mice
ylabel: Share of DS2-to-DS2 intervals under 1 s (Bite line)
why: Complete separation of PTEN from control on the Halo set (every PTEN mouse above every control with a value), P = 0.007 on the No P-spikes set, and the same sign in every sub-contrast. Events in quick succession are a plausible sign of a more excitable dentate.
against: It holds for DS2 under the Bite line classifier only: over all events the same measure shows nothing (P = 0.32), and under other classifiers it is the same sign but rarely under 0.05. Three recordings have no value (the classifier is not eligible there). In one-cloud recordings 'DS2' is an arbitrary part of the events. Treat as the weakest lead here.
test: Define bursts on all dentate spikes with a fixed detection threshold, not on a classifier's DS2.

title: The source is briefer the higher the knockout (DS2 events)
ylabel: Duration of the source between the blades, DS2 median
why: One of the two strongest dose relations by raw P (rho = −0.94 within PTEN), the same sign under all 19 classifiers and on the other event set (P = 0.015). A shorter return current would go with the weaker net source of lead 5: two views of the same change at the granule cell layer.
against: Over all events the relation is not there at P < 0.05; it is specific to the majority type under the optimized classifier, and durations are whole milliseconds, so a few ties decide the rank. Nine mice in two knockout clusters.
test: Take the duration on the mean event per mouse at sub-millisecond resolution (the raw 30 kHz data), all events, one planned Spearman test.
